column1: # Every rule the requirement map applies, and what tests it. A test in
# src/rules.rs checks this table against the code and the files it cites:
# every reason code, edge kind and entry-point kind the map can write, and
# every rule ci/requirement_map.py's check can name (CHECK_RULES), has one
# row, and no row names anything else; every unit test, fixture reading,
# mutation case and sentinel a row cites exists; a code's positive reading and
# sentinel read that code, and its negative does not; a code's mutation moves
# a reading to or from it; a check rule's mutation is a planted case naming it.
#   rule      the code, edge kind, entry-point kind or check rule
#   kind      code | edge | root | check | outcome | pin
#   unit      unit tests in src/ (`;` between several); for a pin state (ci/intent_pins.py),
#   positive  a fixture reading (tools/requirement_map/fixture/expected.tsv) the rule decides;
#             for an outcome, a fixture manifest row (requirement:symbol, intent-expected.tsv)
#   negative  a nearby fixture reading, or manifest row, it does not
#   sentinel  a committed real-tree reading (ci/requirement_map.sentinels.tsv), artifact:path
#   gap       why a column holds `-`; `-` when none does
